name: Product Operations Stage Analysis Rubric
description: Evaluation criteria for a Threat Model Spec Analysis Report produced at the Product Operations PDLC stage.

categories.name: Invariant Drift Detection
categories.description: Whether critical security invariants from Product Definition are actually checked against production reality.

options.label: Pass
criteria: Every critical-criticality SecurityRequirement has a corresponding ArchitectureAssertion checked against production telemetry

options.label: Partial
criteria: Some invariants checked but at least one critical invariant is unaddressed

options.label: Fail
criteria: No invariant drift checks against production data

categories.evaluationPrompt: Is every critical-criticality SecurityRequirement from Product Definition checked against actual production telemetry via an ArchitectureAssertion?

categories.name: Adoption Signal Completeness
categories.description: Whether the report includes adoption/usage signal, not solely incident-driven findings.

options.label: Pass
criteria: Report includes adoption/usage/retention signal alongside any incident findings

options.label: Partial
criteria: Some adoption signal present but thin or disconnected from security invariants

options.label: Fail
criteria: Report is entirely incident-reactive with no adoption/usage signal

categories.evaluationPrompt: Does the report include adoption or usage signal (not just incident data), so an absence of incidents is never mistaken for validated safety?

categories.name: Evidence Grounding
categories.description: Whether findings cite specific telemetry or incident evidence rather than general impressions.

options.label: Pass
criteria: Every Finding cites specific telemetry-query or incident Evidence

options.label: Partial
criteria: Most findings cite evidence but at least one is a general impression

options.label: Fail
criteria: Findings present with no cited evidence

categories.evaluationPrompt: Does every Finding cite a specific Evidence object (a telemetry query or incident record), not a general impression of production behavior?
